entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Tigranes the Younger was an Artaxiad prince who briefly ruled the Kingdom of Sophene in 65 BC. He was the son of Tigranes II and succeeded his father as king after his death in 69 BC. During his reign, Tigranes the Younger faced significant challenges from the Roman Empire, which had been expanding its territories in the region. In 65 BC, he sent an embassy to Rome, hoping to secure a peace treaty. However, the Romans were unwilling to negotiate with him, and instead, they occupied Sophene and forced Tigranes to abdicate. This marked the end of Artaxid rule in Sophene and paved the way for Roman dominance in the region. Despite his brief reign, Tigranes the Younger left a lasting legacy as one of the last independent rulers of Sophene. His story serves as a reminder of the complexities of ancient geopolitics and the often-violent nature of statecraft.
